programmes.d: Clare has a serious dilemma that will affect her entire future and confides in Alli and Jenna.

Abstinence-pledged Darcy wakes up in a strange bed, screamingly hung-over. Panic-stricken, she tries to piece together the events of the night before. She knows – physically – she had sex, but everything else is a blank.
Drew's not taking the easy way out - he's going to be part of his child's life, whether Clare wants it or not.
Paige is ecstatic to have landed herself a gig in the fashion world. If everything goes well, this could turn itself into a brand new career path.
Frankie isn't a little girl anymore!
After seeing Craig’s newly released album on the shelves at the record store, Ashley decides to pursue her own music – starting with a performance at the Lakehurst-Degrassi talent mixer.
Clare has to muster up the courage to tell Eli about her situation.

Amidst the crowded classrooms and the battle for school territory, tensions between Lakehurst and Degrassi students continue to mount. But Spinner’s got his eye on enemy territory -- the adorably tough new Lakehurst girl, Jane.
Becky and her brother Luke’s relationship is very strained.
Faced with his own aggression and looming mortality, Spinner attempts to prove his ‘masculinity’ by kicking an unnecessary amount of Lakehurst ass.
Maya can’t sleep. She’s having nightmares about Miles’ safety, and they’re becoming all too familiar.

Manny’s moved back home but the honeymoon between she and her parents is just about over. And when her dad insists she have a traditional “Debut” – the lavish party many Filipino girls have for their 18th birthday – Manny takes a stand.
When Zoë lands her dream role, it hits a little too close to home following her assault.
Fireworks begin at Wild Wild West Night when Clare makes her decision known with regards to Drew and Eli.

Ellie’s ex-mentor Caitlin Ryan arrives to do a guest lecture series in Jesse’s class and Ellie sees her opportunity to set herself apart from her peers. She throws herself into Caitlin’s class assignment and her hard work quickly pays off.
Maya is doing her best to keep Zig safe but when she finds a bag of drugs, her worst fears are confirmed.

Emma decides she’ll do what it takes to get back on track, starting by rekindling her friendship with Manny, but when Manny wants to hit an audition to be a ‘Purple Dragon’ sports drink model, Emma finds herself quickly at odds with her best friend.
Hiding Zig out at the Matlin house while the Maya organizes the Art Night seems to be working… for now.
Spinner deals with chemo, timing how long he can go between barf-buckets, while his cheerleader Jane, tries to bring the party to him.
Becky feels isolated at home since helping turn in her brother.

Marco and Ellie’s retail therapy goes awry when Marco finds his credit card maxed out. Ellie rescues him this time, but Marco realizes a new job is the real solution—and might even give him the opportunity to meet new people.
Drew was fired from the campaign, his friends think he’s a home-wrecker, and he’s in a fight with Dallas.
Roofie rape victim Darcy is barreling down a self-destructive path and only a handful of people know why.
When Tristan asks Mr. Yates for some help, Mr. Yates suggests he come to his apartment for some extra help.
Manny and Jay’s faux-mance is working perfectly. But when Jay gets too serious, Manny reminds him it's all fake.
Tristan is warned by Mr. Yates to make his feelings about their affair less obvious at school.
Zoë's trial begins and she fears that she is being painted in a harsh light.

After Manny discovers that her University demo reel is actually a sex tape that she and Jay made, her future hangs in the balance. By the time Jay catches up to her with the correct DVD, it's too late.
The media is abuzz about Zoë’s trial.
When cute and funny Rachel joins Peter, Danny & Derek’s MI group for their “How-To” video project, confidence is high.
Will a superstorm headed for Toronto stall a Degrassi dance?
Mia’s finally been granted a spot on Spirit Squad, and she’s ecstatic. But trying to be a normal teenager is proving a difficult balancing act.
Clare is forced to spend the night with Eli while in New York City.
Paige is on her A game - she's excelling at work, Andrea's given her a raise, and she’s going to use the money to redesign her bedroom.
Clare has a serious dilemma that will affect her entire future and confides in Alli and Jenna.

Since Snake’s suspension from teaching, Emma’s life has been turned upside-down. He’s really in a funk, and the dark cloud over his head has fouled the air at home, where Emma finds herself caught in the no-man’s-land between her parents.
Drew's not taking the easy way out - he's going to be part of his child's life, whether Clare wants it or not.

Jimmy finally gets the news he’s been waiting for – he’s been accepted into NYU! But he’s got other things on his mind. He is slowly discovering that he has other options when it comes to his real dream – walking again.
Frankie isn't a little girl anymore!

It’s Anya’s first year running the Free The Children Freedom Fast to promote education and health in Africa. She has a lot to coordinate - which would be hard enough without meddling Holly J, who’s determined to make Anya choose between her and Sav.
Clare has to muster up the courage to tell Eli about her situation.
Becky and her brother Luke’s relationship is very strained.

Mia’s renewed relationship with Lucas is making her feel like she’s on top of the world. With the extra free time afforded by his help, she's taking on all the high school things her parenting has kept her from enjoying.
Maya can’t sleep. She’s having nightmares about Miles’ safety, and they’re becoming all too familiar.
Marco’s world is rocked when Paige drops a bomb – her dad’s going to help her buy a condo. Ellie’s just learned she might be up for the editorship of the Core newspaper, so she’s distracted.
Zoë receives threatening texts from an unknown number
Spinner and Jimmy have just one more exam before they’re finally done school and, with Jimmy's help, Spinner's sure he can pass and enjoy his cancer-free future.
Tristan organizes an intervention for Miles, but it only pushes him further away.
With time ticking towards the Class of ’07 Prom and Graduation ceremony, Liberty has the perfect night planned: a hotel prom, with the amazing Natasha Bedingfield performing.
Drew is committed to keeping Becky happy but his situation with Clare has his attention divided.

Relieved of parental duty for the year by mom, Mia starts the school year off with a bang by bonding with new girl, Leia, and getting scouted to be the new face of football star Tom Blakes’ shoe line.
Mr. Simpson calls an assembly to address the offending fundraising website.
Mia does what she can to ensure her success. Besides, Tom is handsome and famous, so Mia thinks being with Tom to get ahead isn’t such a bad trade.
Degrassi's fundraising scandal threatens to ruin Frankie's relationship with her father.
Mr. Hollingsworth’s campaign is in its final stretch, and the stress has him even more tense than usual.

Jane wants to play football but since there is no girls team, then boys’ football it is. The Shep doesn’t like the idea one bit, but once Jane proves she’s faster, stronger, and more athletic than most of the team, he relents…
Degrassi is now in the hands of a new, strict Administrator which means new, strict rules.

Eager to make the most of her college experience, Liberty jumps at the chance to rush the most popular sorority at Smithdale. Determined to get in, Liberty slowly exchanges old habits and old friends (Manny and Emma) for sorority approved ones.
Winston is set to play the lead in his musical but is not pleased that Lola could star opposite him.
Peter begins a relationship with Mia and a friendship with Riley. Finding a balance between a new girlfriend and a new guy friend gets confusing, especially when Riley is suddenly kissing Peter.
It’s Frankie’s birthday, and she’s going to celebrate it, Hollingsworth style -- with a Gatsby party!

Sav and Anya plan to celebrate their six-month anniversary on the school’s overnight trip. Only problem? Alli, Sav’s sister, convinces their parents to let her go on the trip on the condition that Sav spends every second with her.
Zoe is facing jail time following the fundraising scandal
Mia’s T-Bombz campaign is hitting the city and Degrassi. But Holly J has bigger and better things going on. She’s prepping the Power Squad for an out-of-town competition, and things are looking good.
Becky has feelings for Jonah, but she isn't sure what to do with them.
Spinner and Jane have plans for next year – she’ll start pre-law and he’ll attend Police College. When he doesn’t get in, he can’t bear to tell her, so he lies.
Maya has someone on her mind, and is questioning the house rules Mrs. Matlin has set.
Prom is fast approaching, but Clare is MIA from committee meetings.
Desperate to win Jane back, Spinner sneaks into the Leadership Convention Jane is speaking at and proposes. When Jane turns him down, Spinner breaks up with her – nothing he does is ever good enough.
Zig is hesitant to let Maya see his new place.
Riley’s the star of Degrassi’s first-ever football game win! The Shep is floored at how much Riley’s improved.
Zig learns the truth behind some recent events, and now he’s an accomplice to a crime.

Clare stands up for Connor when he receives unfair treatment from The Shep. The result of their peaceful protest? Detentions for everyone. No one is more frustrated by the detention than Alli. It wasn’t her idea to protest.
